newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $65 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $65 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Tuesday were slow, with light sales reported in Kansas at $65.00 per cwt, unchanged from thin activity on Monday, feedlot sources said.
About 1,700 head sold in Kansas, sources there said. There were no reports yet of sales in the Texas Panhandle or western Oklahoma area, Texas sources said.
Packers were bidding $65.00 against asking levels that mostly ranged from $66.00 to $68.00, they said.
There still was optimism that the bulk of this week's sales would be at $66.00, some sources said.

Prices were expected to be underpinned by an early winter cold blast overnight in the Plains states which sent temperatures plummeting to single digits and spawned wind chills of minus 20 degrees Fahrenheit, feedlot sources said.
Frigid weather is expected to last possibly into next week. Cattle weight gains were seen curbed by the cold.
Fed cattle prices also were expected to be supported by firm beef demand for fill-in buying before the Christmas and New Years holidays and for planned post-holiday features, market sources said.
